sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a house in Greenfield?
sections.html:
A Greenfield homeowner can list with an agent, sell without one, or take a cash offer from a buyer who purchases the house as it is. The city lies in Milwaukee County, and the Census Bureau estimates 37,159 residents as of July 1, 2025, compared with 37,803 counted in the 2020 census.

Listing makes sense when the house is updated and you can wait through showings. A direct sale fits an owner with a dated kitchen, deferred repairs, a vacant house or an estate to settle. Both routes finish at the Milwaukee County Register of Deeds with the same fee and return.

Greenfield is a built-out suburb on Milwaukee's southwest side, covering 11.5 square miles with the Root River running through its western part. The ZIP codes are 53219, 53220, 53221 and 53228. Wikipedia calls it one of many bedroom communities in the Milwaukee metropolitan area, and the Census density of 3,278 people per square mile fits that description.

The land began as the town of Kinnikennick, created in 1839 and renamed Greenfield in 1841. Over the decades surrounding communities incorporated and took pieces of the town. When Greenfield incorporated as a city in 1957 it was the last municipality in Milwaukee County to do so, at about a third of its original size.

Getting around is straightforward. Interstates 41 and 43 serve the city, and Milwaukee County Transit routes 24, 28, 35, 55, 60, 76 and 92 run through it. The Powerline Trail, which opened in 2022, gives walkers and cyclists a path across the city. Because sellers here compete with other Milwaukee suburbs, the highway and bus access is worth listing prominently.

sections.h2: Who buys and sells houses in Greenfield?
sections.html:
The population is older than in most cities of its size. The 2020 census gave a median age of 43.1, with 22.7 percent of residents 65 or older, and 37.6 percent of households were one person living alone. Of 18,035 housing units, 3.8 percent were vacant, and the homeowner vacancy rate was 0.9 percent.

That profile produces a steady flow of sellers who are downsizing, moving closer to family or settling an estate, and of buyers who want a house in the Milwaukee area without a downtown price. About 89.2 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so a typical Greenfield owner has been in the home long enough that the kitchen, bathrooms and mechanicals may be original.

The School District of Greenfield serves families with Greenfield High School and Greenfield Middle School, and it runs 4K and 5K early learning programs. The district has also maintained a referendum website, a good reminder to check the school tax portion of the bill when you compare Greenfield with a neighboring district.

sections.h2: What should a Greenfield seller ask the city before listing?
sections.html:
Ask the City of Greenfield Inspection Services office whether any permit on the property is still open, and whether a past addition, finished basement or deck has a final inspection on record. An open permit surfaces during a buyer's due diligence and tends to slow or end a conventional sale. A direct buyer will usually take the file as it stands, but the question still belongs on your list.

  • Open building, electrical or plumbing permits and final inspections.
  • Any orders from the city about the exterior, such as a fence or accessory building.
  • Special assessments on the tax bill for street or utility work.
  • Rental or occupancy status if tenants live in the house.

The same office can tell you which projects need a permit if you plan to make repairs before selling.

sections.h2: How does transferring a Greenfield house work, and what does it cost?
sections.html:
Greenfield lies in Milwaukee County, so the deed is recorded at the Milwaukee County Register of Deeds, 901 N. 9th Street, Room 103, Milwaukee, open 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. on weekdays. The office records and indexes real estate documents and collects the real estate transfer tax. Wisconsin sets the fee at 30 cents for each $100 of value or fraction thereof, charged to the seller, so a $260,000 sale carries $780 (Wis. Stat. 77.22).

The statute also exempts a list of transfers, including transfers by will, descent or survivorship, transfers from a parent to a child for nominal consideration, and foreclosure deeds to the mortgage holder (Wis. Stat. 77.25). Milwaukee County offers a free Property Fraud Alert service, which notifies a registered owner when the exact name is listed as grantor or grantee on a recorded document. Sellers who still own other property may find it useful.

sections.h2: What disclosures and property taxes apply when selling in Greenfield?
sections.html:
An owner who sells a one-to-four unit property delivers a completed Real Estate Condition Report within 10 days after the contract is accepted. A buyer who gets it late may rescind within two business days after the tenth day and get the deposit back (Wis. Stat. 709.02). A personal representative, trustee or other court-supervised fiduciary who has never lived in the house is excused.

The general property tax bill is paid in two equal installments, January 31 and July 31, except that a municipality can authorize three or more installments by ordinance, with at least half paid by April 30 and the balance by July 31 (Wis. Stat. 74.11 and 74.12). The next due date is January 31, 2027. Ask the City of Greenfield treasurer for the amount remaining so the title company can prorate it correctly.

faqs.q: Which county records a Greenfield, WI deed?
faqs.a: Milwaukee County. The Register of Deeds is at 901 N. 9th Street, Room 103, in Milwaukee, and it records real estate documents and collects the transfer tax.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer fee on a Greenfield sale?
faqs.a: It is 30 cents for each $100 of value or fraction thereof, paid by the seller. On a $240,000 house that is $720. Transfers by will or descent and some family transfers are exempt under Wis. Stat. 77.25.

faqs.q: Is Greenfield a good place to sell a house in Wisconsin?
faqs.a: Census data put the median owner-occupied value at $261,100, the highest of Kenosha, Janesville, La Crosse and Greenfield, and the city has highway and bus access across the Milwaukee area. Condition and price against recent Greenfield sales decide the outcome on any one house.

faqs.q: Do I need to fix a Greenfield house before selling?
faqs.a: Wisconsin does not require repairs, but a seller covered by chapter 709 must disclose known defects on the condition report. Buyers who purchase as is take on the work themselves, which can save an owner the cost and time of contractors.

faqs.q: When is Greenfield property tax due?
faqs.a: Wisconsin real estate tax is due January 31 and July 31 in two equal installments unless the municipality has adopted an ordinance allowing three or more. Ask the city treasurer for the exact amount and dates on your bill.
